description: What has actually been demonstrated or measured for living off the land on Mars: oxygen production, regolith chemistry, agriculture trials. Engineering tier = demonstrated performance, not a fact about Mars.

facts.label: MOXIE peak oxygen production rate
facts.instrument: Perseverance MOXIE (solid oxide electrolysis of CO2)
facts.notes: At >=98% purity. Design goal was 6-10 g/h. Power-limited by a 4 A supply; the instrument draws roughly 300 W during a run. Use for scaling: a crew of 4 needs ~3.3 kg O2/day; NASA's full-scale concept targets 2-3 kg/h.

facts.label: Total oxygen produced over the MOXIE campaign (16 runs)
facts.notes: First run sol 60 (20 Apr 2021) produced 5.4 g in ~1 h at 751 Pa, 201 K ambient.

facts.label: Perchlorate content of soil at the Phoenix site (68 N)

uncertainty.note: 'a few tenths of a percent' in all three samples; WCL leachate ~2.4 mM ClO4-

facts.label: Perchlorate is present globally in Martian regolith
facts.notes: Detected by Phoenix (WCL) and inferred from Curiosity SAM evolved-gas chlorine releases at Gale. Toxic to humans (thyroid) at these levels; must be removed or the regolith must not be used for food crops. Remediation (washing, microbial perchlorate reduction) is a scenario assumption, not a demonstrated capability.

facts.label: Crop growth in NASA JSC-1A Mars regolith simulant (Earth greenhouse)
facts.value: 9 of 10 crops produced edible biomass comparable to Earth potting soil control; spinach failed; radish, rye, cress produced viable seed
facts.notes: IMPORTANT CAVEATS the agent must carry into any model: (1) JSC-1A contains no perchlorate; (2) grown under Earth gravity, pressure, light and CO2; (3) simulant was amended with organic matter. This supports 'regolith can be a substrate', not 'Mars soil grows food'. Crop yield under Mars light (~43% of Earth TOA, further cut by dust) is an open modeling question.

facts.label: Depth to shallow ice where SWIM finds it consistent (northern mid-latitudes)

uncertainty.note: SWIM distinguishes <5 m and >5 m zones; depth is site-dependent

facts.notes: Candidate human landing regions (Arcadia, Utopia, Deuteronilus) are chosen for this. If the product adds a second region, pick one of these so water ISRU becomes a real design space.

facts.label: Atmospheric water column

uncertainty.note: strong seasonal and latitudinal variation; MCD provides columns

facts.notes: Extracting water from Mars air means processing ~10^5 m^3 of air per litre. Technically possible, energetically terrible. Any module claiming atmospheric water harvest must show the energy budget.
